name: King of Tappuah
overview: The King of Tappuah was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. Scripture does not specify his tribal affiliation or provide additional personal details. His role is noted solely in the context of this military defeat.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Tappuah' directly denotes his position as the monarch over the city or region of Tappuah. The name is a straightforward designation without further linguistic or theological significance beyond indicating his rulership, as presented in Joshua 12:17.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Tappuah beyond his identification as a defeated king in Joshua 12:17. There are no listed relatives or alliances associated with him.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Tappuah's importance lies in his inclusion among the thirty-one kings subdued by Joshua, marking the fulfillment of God's promise to give Israel victory over the land. His defeat represents God's sovereign hand in establishing Israel's possession of Canaan, underscoring the divine authority behind Joshua's conquest.
